sourceTitle: The Functional Role of Dreaming in Emotional Processes
author: Luigi De Gennaro, Serena Scarpelli, Valentina Alfonsi, Maurizio Gorgoni
chapter: Frontiers in Psychology: Emotional Memory and Sleep
text: Dream experience (DE) is intrinsically linked to emotional processes and the human inner world. Both rapid eye movement (REM) and non-REM (NREM) sleep stages support emotional memory consolidation and emotion regulation. Electroencephalographic (EEG) investigations show that human sleep patterns—specifically fronto-temporal theta oscillations during REM sleep and slow wave activity during NREM—modulate how emotionally charged waking experiences are reprocessed, integrated into long-term autobiographical memory networks, and depotentiated of their acute distress.

sourceTitle: The Functional Role of Dreaming in Emotional Processes
author: Luigi De Gennaro, Serena Scarpelli, Valentina Alfonsi, Maurizio Gorgoni
text: A critical cognitive function of dreaming is emotional depotentiation: dreams allow the brain to reactivate affective memory traces in a neurochemically safe environment (characterized by low noradrenergic tone during REM sleep), thereby decoupling emotional intensity from episodic memory content. When this regulatory mechanism fails, individuals experience recurrent, disruptive nightmares, chronic hyperarousal, and emotional dysregulation, commonly observed in post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and sleep disorders.
